examples.ko: 저명한 교수님이 우리 학교에서 강연을 해요.
examples.en: A renowned professor gives a lecture at our school.
This hospital has many eminent doctors.
That writer is renowned abroad too.
Renowned scholars gathered in one place.
The painter was not well known, but the paintings were wonderful.
I got very nervous meeting such a prominent person.

explain: '유명하다'는 일상에서 누구에게나 쓰지만, '저명하다'는 학자·작가·의사처럼 사회적으로 인정받는 사람에게 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 말할 때보다 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 보통 '저명한 + 사람'처럼 사람 앞에서 꾸며 줘요.
explain_en: '유명하다' is for anyone or anything famous in daily talk, while '저명하다' is a formal word for people society respects, such as scholars, writers, and doctors. You see it more in news and writing than in speech. It usually modifies a person: '저명한 + person'.

examples.en: I was busy all day entertaining guests.

examples.ko: 거래처 사람들을 접대해야 해서 오늘 저녁에 약속이 있어요.
examples.en: I have to entertain clients, so I have plans this evening.

examples.ko: 부장님이 손님을 접대하는 자리에 저도 갔어요.
examples.en: I also went to the dinner where our department head was hosting a guest.
We hosted the relatives who came to our house with great care.
I started preparing the food to serve the guests in the morning.
We keep the costs of entertaining at the company in a separate record.

explain: '대접하다'는 가족이나 친구에게도 쓰지만, '접대하다'는 일 때문에 만난 손님이나 거래처를 모실 때 자주 써요. 그래서 회사 이야기에 많이 나와요. '접대비', '접대 자리'처럼 단어를 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: '대접하다' can be used for family and friends too, but '접대하다' is often used for guests or business partners you meet for work, so it appears a lot in office talk. It also forms words such as '접대비' (entertainment expenses) and '접대 자리' (an entertaining occasion).

en: reinforcement; strengthening (of staff, equipment, or capacity)

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 보안 인력 증강을 계획해요.
examples.en: The company plans to increase its security staff this year.

examples.ko: 서버 증강 작업 때문에 사이트가 잠시 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The site stopped for a while because of the server upgrade work.
Expanding equipment costs a lot of money.
I asked the team leader to add more staff.

examples.ko: 이번 증강으로 처리 속도가 두 배 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: With this expansion, the processing speed doubled.

examples.ko: 증강이 끝나면 더 많은 손님을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once the expansion is done, we can take more customers.

explain: '증강'은 이미 있는 인력, 장비, 능력을 더 크게 보태는 일에 써요. '증가'는 숫자가 늘어난다는 결과에 쓰고, '증강'은 일부러 늘려 힘을 키운다는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스와 회사 문서에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '증강' is for deliberately adding to existing staff, equipment, or capacity. '증가' just describes a number going up, while '증강' feels like building up strength on purpose. It shows up often in news and company documents.

examples.en: The company upgraded its servers, so it got faster.

examples.ko: 소방서에서 야간 근무 인력을 증강하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The fire station decided to add more night-shift staff.
Our team is going to add more people.
The hospital strengthened its emergency room equipment.

examples.ko: 겨울에 대비해 난방 설비를 증강하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are expanding the heating equipment to prepare for winter.

examples.ko: 인력을 증강하는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to build up staff.

explain: '증강하다'는 목적어로 '인력', '장비', '설비'처럼 힘이 되는 것을 써요. '늘리다'보다 딱딱하고 계획해서 키운다는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 보고서에서 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: '증강하다' takes objects that add strength, such as '인력', '장비', and '설비'. It is stiffer than '늘리다' and suggests planned build-up. It is more common in news and reports than in everyday conversation.

examples.en: I can't stand bugs.
My younger sibling can't stand spicy food.
My father really hates being late.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 신발이 젖는 건 질색이에요.
examples.en: I hate it when my shoes get wet on rainy days.
I hate cleaning, but I have to do it today.
My friend can't stand lies, so my friend is always honest.

explain: '싫어하다'보다 훨씬 강하게, 보기만 해도 몸이 움츠러들 정도로 싫을 때 써요. 보통 '~라면 질색이다'나 '~(은/는) 질색이다'처럼 말해요. 가볍게 말하는 구어에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '싫어하다': you recoil just at the thought of something. People usually say '~라면 질색이다' or '~(은/는) 질색이다'. It comes up often in casual speech.

en: hate; be disgusted by; recoil from

examples.en: My older sister recoils at the sight of bugs.
My mother can't stand lies.
I used to hate crowded places.
My friend hates karaoke, so we don't go.
They looked at me with a repelled expression.
The smell was so bad it made people recoil.

explain: '질색하다'는 '싫어하다'와 달리 몸으로 느끼는 거부감이 커요. '질색을 하다'로도 쓰고, 뜻은 거의 같아요. 사람이 주어이고, 싫은 대상은 '을/를'로 받아요.
explain_en: Unlike '싫어하다', '질색하다' carries a physical sense of recoiling. '질색을 하다' means almost the same. A person is the subject and the thing disliked takes '을/를'.

examples.en: The parents observed the class.
I am going to the court tomorrow to observe a trial.
Teachers observe classes at other schools.

examples.ko: 공장 견학에서 작업 과정을 참관할 수 있어요.
examples.en: On the factory tour, you can observe the work process.
The person who observed the exam wrote a confirmation.
You have to stay quiet while you observe.

explain: '참관하다'는 직접 하지 않고 그 자리에 있으면서 지켜보는 거예요. '구경하다'는 재미로 보는 것이고, '참관하다'는 공식적인 자리나 일을 볼 때 써요. '수업 참관', '재판 참관'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: With '참관하다' you are present and watching without taking part. '구경하다' is looking for fun, while '참관하다' is for official events or work. It is also common as a noun: '수업 참관' (class observation), '재판 참관' (trial observation).

examples.ko: 그 나라의 통치자는 오랫동안 바뀌지 않았어요.
examples.en: The ruler of that country did not change for a long time.
I read stories about ancient rulers in a history book.

examples.ko: 좋은 통치자는 국민의 이야기를 잘 들어요.
examples.en: A good ruler listens well to the people.
When the ruler changed, the mood of the country changed too.
That king is remembered as a wise ruler.
The ruler in the drama was a frightening person.

explain: '통치자'는 나라나 지역을 다스리는 사람을 넓게 가리켜요. '왕', '황제', '대통령'처럼 정해진 직함이 아니라 역할을 말할 때 편해요. 역사 이야기나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: '통치자' broadly refers to whoever governs a country or region. It is handy when you mean the role rather than a fixed title like '왕', '황제', or '대통령'. You see it often in history and news.

en: submit (an article or letter) to a newspaper or magazine

examples.en: I sent my thoughts to a newspaper.
I am going to submit a photo to a magazine.
There is a section where readers submit their opinions.
I submitted my paper to an academic journal and am waiting for the result.
The piece I submitted last week was published today.
To submit a piece, you have to send it by email.

explain: '투고하다'는 신문, 잡지, 학회지 같은 곳에 요청받지 않고 먼저 글을 보내는 거예요. 회사에 서류를 내는 '제출하다'와 달리 실리기를 바라는 글에 써요. '독자 투고', '투고 원고'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: '투고하다' means sending a piece of writing to a newspaper, magazine, or journal on your own initiative, hoping it will be published. Unlike '제출하다' (hand in), it is for writing meant to be printed. Common terms: '독자 투고' (reader contribution), '투고 원고' (submitted manuscript).

examples.en: The baby burped after drinking milk.
I burp often when I drink soda.
It is rude to burp during a meal.

examples.ko: 아기가 트림할 때까지 등을 두드려 주세요.
examples.en: Pat the baby's back until the baby burps.
After I burped, my stomach felt better.
I was embarrassed because I burped in front of a friend.

explain: 한국에서는 어른이 사람들 앞에서 트림하면 예의 없다고 느끼는 경우가 많아요. 반대로 아기는 우유를 먹은 뒤에 트림을 시켜 줘야 해서 '트림시키다'라는 말을 써요. '트림을 하다'라고 띄어 써도 뜻이 같아요.
explain_en: In Korea, burping in front of others as an adult is often seen as impolite. For babies, though, you help them burp after feeding, which is '트림시키다'. Writing '트림을 하다' with a space means the same.

examples.ko: 그 가게의 영업 행태가 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The way that shop does business became a problem.

examples.ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들의 소비 행태를 조사했어요.
examples.en: We surveyed the spending patterns of young people these days.

examples.ko: 운전 중에 휴대폰을 보는 행태는 위험해요.
examples.en: Looking at a phone while driving is dangerous behavior.
If this kind of behavior continues, you lose trust.
I observed the behavior of animals for a long time.
The employees protested against the company's unfair conduct.

explain: '행동'은 한 번의 움직임에도 쓰지만, '행태'는 반복되는 모습이나 방식을 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '소비 행태', '영업 행태'처럼 많이 쓰고, 좋지 않은 모습을 말할 때가 많아요. 칭찬할 때는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: '행동' can describe a single action, but '행태' is for a repeated pattern or way of behaving. It appears in phrases like '소비 행태' (spending pattern) and '영업 행태' (business practice), and often points to something undesirable. It is rarely used for praise.

examples.en: If you pay late, a surcharge is added.
If you have a certificate, you get bonus points.
An extra amount was added to the tax.
The amount rose a lot because an addition was applied.
Night work comes with an added allowance.

examples.ko: 이 경우에는 가산 없이 그대로 계산해요.
examples.en: In this case, we calculate it as it is, with nothing added.

explain: '가산'은 원래 금액이나 점수에 따로 더하는 것을 말해요. 일반 '더하기'가 아니라 규칙에 따라 붙는 추가분이라는 느낌이에요. '가산점', '가산세', '가산 수당'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '가산' is an amount or score added on top of the original one. Rather than plain addition, it feels like an extra portion applied by a rule. It forms terms like '가산점' (bonus points), '가산세' (penalty tax), and '가산 수당' (premium pay).

en: add on; add as an extra amount

examples.en: We calculate it by adding interest for the number of days late.
We decided to add points for certificates.
This is the amount with the fee added.
Check the rules when you add points.
Volunteer hours are added to the grade.

examples.ko: 야간 근무에는 수당을 가산하는 회사가 많아요.
examples.en: Many companies add an allowance for night work.

explain: '더하다'는 어디에나 쓰지만, '가산하다'는 기준이 되는 값에 규칙에 따라 추가분을 얹을 때 써요. 수수료, 이자, 점수처럼 계산할 수 있는 것과 잘 어울려요. 말보다 문서에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: '더하다' works anywhere, but '가산하다' is for adding an extra portion by rule onto a base value. It pairs well with calculable things such as fees, interest, and points. You see it in documents more than in speech.

en: become heavier; be aggravated; intensify (of a burden)

examples.en: The burden got heavier because the work increased.

examples.ko: 이자가 올라서 생활비 부담이 가중되고 있어요.
examples.en: The burden of living costs is growing heavier because interest went up.
As patients increase, the fatigue of the medical staff intensifies.
I'm worried that my responsibility will become heavier.

examples.ko: 날씨 때문에 교통 혼잡이 더 가중됐어요.
examples.en: The traffic jam got even worse because of the weather.
I started exercising to reduce the growing stress.

explain: '가중되다'는 이미 힘든 부담, 책임, 피로 같은 것이 더 무거워질 때 써요. '늘어나다'와 달리 나쁜 쪽으로 더해진다는 느낌이 강해요. 주어는 '부담', '피로', '책임'처럼 짐이 되는 말이 와요.
explain_en: '가중되다' is used when an already heavy burden, responsibility, or fatigue gets heavier. Unlike '늘어나다', it strongly suggests things piling up in a bad direction. The subject is usually something burdensome: '부담', '피로', '책임'.

examples.en: I felt humiliated being criticized in front of people.
I was humiliated over a small mistake.

examples.ko: 그 굴욕을 아직도 잊을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I still can't forget that humiliation.
I bore the humiliation and worked until the end.
Being teased in front of my friends was humiliating.
That team suffered a humiliating defeat.

explain: '창피'는 내 실수 때문에 부끄러운 것이고, '굴욕'은 남에게 무시당하거나 억눌려서 자존심이 상하는 거예요. '굴욕을 당하다', '굴욕을 느끼다'처럼 써요. 형용사처럼 쓸 때는 '굴욕적이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '창피' is embarrassment over your own mistake, while '굴욕' is a wounded pride from being looked down on or forced into submission. Typical verbs: '굴욕을 당하다', '굴욕을 느끼다'. As an adjective, use '굴욕적이다'.

examples.en: The reporter gave commentary on the game results.
An expert comments on the new policy.
I wrote a post commenting on a movie on my blog.
I said I'm not in a position to comment right now.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 발표를 짧게 논평해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher gave a short comment on my presentation.
I read what the newspaper commented.

explain: '논평하다'는 어떤 일이나 작품을 보고 자기 생각과 평가를 말하거나 글로 쓰는 거예요. 일상에서는 '말하다'나 '이야기하다'를 쓰고, '논평하다'는 기자, 전문가, 공식 발표에서 자주 나와요. '논평을 내다', '논평을 거부하다'처럼 명사 '논평'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '논평하다' means giving your view or evaluation of an event or work, in speech or writing. In daily talk people say '말하다' or '이야기하다'; '논평하다' appears with reporters, experts, and official statements. The noun '논평' is common too: '논평을 내다' (issue a comment), '논평을 거부하다' (decline to comment).

examples.en: This computer surpasses the previous model.
My younger brother surpassed our older brother in skill.
The result exceeded expectations.

examples.ko: 맛으로는 이 집이 다른 가게를 능가해요.
examples.en: In taste, this place outdoes the other shops.
The athlete practiced hard to beat the record.

examples.ko: 그분은 제가 능가할 수 없을 만큼 대단한 분이에요.
examples.en: That person is so great that I can't surpass them.

explain: '능가하다'는 비교하는 상대보다 한 수 위라는 뜻으로, 보통 '~을/를 능가하다'로 써요. '이기다'는 경기에서 쓰고, '능가하다'는 실력, 성능, 기대 같은 수준을 비교할 때 써요. '기대를 능가하다'가 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
explain_en: '능가하다' puts something a step above what it is compared with, normally as '~을/를 능가하다'. '이기다' fits competitions, while '능가하다' compares levels such as skill, performance, or expectations. '기대를 능가하다' (exceed expectations) is a common pattern.

examples.en: The expert asserted that this method is safe.

examples.ko: 아직 결과를 모르니까 단언할 수 없어요.
examples.en: We don't know the result yet, so I can't say for sure.

examples.ko: 친구는 내일 꼭 비가 온다고 단언했어요.
examples.en: My friend insisted it will definitely rain tomorrow.
There isn't enough evidence to say so firmly right now.

examples.ko: 그렇게 단언하면 나중에 곤란해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you state it so flatly, you may be in trouble later.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님은 병이 나을 거라고 단언하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The doctor did not guarantee that the illness will get better.

explain: '단언하다'는 '틀림없다'고 확실하게 잘라 말하는 거예요. 그래서 부정형 '단언할 수 없다'를 아주 자주 써요. '말하다'보다 강하고, 말한 사람이 책임을 지는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: '단언하다' is to say flatly that something is certain. That is why the negative '단언할 수 없다' (can't say for sure) is very common. It is stronger than '말하다' and implies the speaker stands behind the claim.

examples.en: The government announced the privatization of the airport.
The fees changed after privatization.
I watched a debate about railway privatization.
The employees were very worried during the privatization process.
News about the bank's privatization came out.

examples.ko: 민영화가 된 뒤에 서비스가 좋아졌다는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say the service improved after privatization.

explain: '민영화'는 나라가 운영하던 회사나 사업을 민간 회사가 맡게 하는 일을 말하는 경제 용어예요. 반대말은 '국유화'예요. 뉴스에서 '공기업 민영화'로 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '민영화' is an economics term for turning a state-run company or business over to private hands. Its opposite is '국유화' (nationalization). You hear it in the news as '공기업 민영화' (privatization of public enterprises).

examples.en: The government decided to privatize that company.
If you privatize a public enterprise, competition grows.
It is a company that was privatized a few years ago.

examples.ko: 민영화할 때 직원들을 어떻게 할지 논의했어요.
examples.en: We discussed what to do with the employees when privatizing.
The city privatized part of its bus service.
The number of countries that privatize is growing.

explain: '민영화하다'는 주어가 보통 정부나 국가예요. 같은 일을 당하는 쪽에서 말하려면 '민영화되다'를 써요. '사유화하다'는 개인이 차지한다는 뜻이라서 달라요.
explain_en: The subject of '민영화하다' is usually the government or the state. From the side that receives it, use '민영화되다'. '사유화하다' differs: it means an individual takes it as private property.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 변장하고 도시를 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie walks around the city in disguise.
A disguised police officer waited for the criminal at the market.
I dressed up as a witch for Halloween.
Even with sunglasses and a hat as a disguise, I recognized the person right away.
The children dressed up as animals and took photos.
The disguise was so perfect that nobody knew.

explain: '변장'은 다른 사람인 척하려고 옷이나 겉모습을 바꾸는 일이에요. '분장'은 연극이나 영화처럼 역할을 위해 꾸미는 거라서 다르고, '변장'은 정체를 숨기거나 속일 때 써요. 보통 '변장하다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: '변장' means changing your clothes or look to pass as someone else. '분장' is made up for a role, as in a play or film, while '변장' is for hiding or deceiving about identity. It is mostly used as the verb '변장하다'.

en: be lost; be destroyed (by fire, disaster, etc.)

examples.en: Old documents were lost in the fire.
The file was lost, so I started over from the beginning.
We are recovering the lost data.
Many cultural properties were destroyed during the war.
Back it up so the data is not lost.
The village houses almost burned down in the wildfire.

explain: '소실되다'는 불, 사고, 오류 때문에 있던 것이 없어지는 거예요. '잃어버리다'는 내가 물건을 놓친 것이고, '소실되다'는 자료, 건물, 문화재처럼 되찾기 어려운 것에 써요. 말할 때보다 기사나 공문서에 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '소실되다' means something that existed is gone due to fire, an accident, or an error. '잃어버리다' is you losing an item; '소실되다' is for things like data, buildings, or cultural property that are hard to get back. It appears in articles and official documents more than in speech.

examples.en: The cat takes a nap in a sunny spot.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 양지바른 곳에 앉아 있고 싶어요.
examples.en: In winter, I want to sit in a sunny place.
I hung the laundry out in a sunny spot.
This house gets sun, so it is warm even in winter.
My grandmother dries beans in a sunny spot.
Plants grow better in the sun than in the shade.

explain: '양지'의 반대말은 '음지'로, 햇볕이 드는 곳과 그늘진 곳을 구분할 때 써요. '양지바르다'는 햇빛이 잘 드는 곳을 묘사하는 말이에요. '양지'는 따뜻하고 좋은 곳이라는 느낌이 있어서, 편한 처지를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: The opposite of '양지' is '음지' (shade): sunny spots versus shaded ones. '양지바르다' describes a place that gets plenty of sun. Because '양지' feels warm and good, it can also stand figuratively for a comfortable position.

en: the others; the rest; other (as a modifier)

examples.ko: 이 가게는 여타 가게보다 값이 싸요.
examples.en: This shop is cheaper than other shops.
We'll talk about the other issues tomorrow.
I'm good at English, but not at other foreign languages.
I'll tell you the remaining items separately.
The rest of the students have already gone home.
The rules are different in other cases.

explain: '여타'는 '그 밖의 나머지'를 말하고, 보통 명사 앞에서 '여타 + 명사'로 써요. '다른'보다 딱딱하고 글에 더 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '나머지'나 '다른'을 써도 충분해요.
explain_en: '여타' means 'everything else' and is usually placed before a noun: '여타 + noun'. It is stiffer than '다른' and appears more in writing. In everyday talk, '나머지' or '다른' work fine.

en: view; read; look through (documents or records)

examples.en: I looked through old newspapers at the library.
To view the documents, you have to submit an application.
You can view the certificate online.
There is a rule that only employees view this material.

examples.ko: 자료를 열람하는 동안 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos while viewing the material.
Please sign after you look over the contract.

explain: '열람하다'는 도서관, 관공서, 회사처럼 정해진 곳에서 자료나 서류를 확인하며 읽는 거예요. '읽다'와 달리 허락이나 절차가 있다는 느낌이 있어요. '열람실', '열람 신청'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '열람하다' is checking and reading materials or documents at a set place such as a library, public office, or company. Unlike '읽다', it suggests permission or procedure. Common terms: '열람실' (reading room), '열람 신청' (viewing request).

examples.en: My grandfather has dignity even without speaking.
The king entered with a majestic stride.

examples.ko: 사자는 위엄 있는 모습으로 서 있어요.
examples.en: The lion stands with a majestic look.

examples.ko: 새 교장 선생님은 위엄을 지키려고 노력해요.
examples.en: The new principal tries to keep an air of authority.
You can feel a sense of grandeur from that old building.
I practiced speaking with authority.

explain: '위엄'은 사람이나 대상에서 느껴지는, 함부로 대하기 어려운 무게감이에요. '위엄 있다', '위엄을 지키다'처럼 써요. '권위'와 비슷하지만 '위엄'은 겉모습이나 태도에서 느껴지는 힘에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: '위엄' is the weight a person or thing carries that makes it hard to treat lightly. Use it as '위엄 있다' or '위엄을 지키다'. Close to '권위', but '위엄' leans toward the power felt in appearance and manner.

en: improper collusion; corrupt alliance; close ties

examples.en: News came out about collusion between politicians and companies.

examples.ko: 부정한 유착을 끊어야 한다고 사람들이 말해요.
examples.en: People say improper ties must be cut off.

examples.ko: 조사 결과 두 회사 사이에 유착은 없었어요.
examples.en: The investigation found no collusion between the two companies.
The deep collusive relationship became a problem.

examples.ko: 유착 의혹을 받은 공무원이 조사를 받았어요.
examples.en: The official suspected of collusion was investigated.
When oversight is weak, collusion arises easily.

explain: '유착'은 서로 붙어서 잘못된 이익을 나누는 관계를 말해서, 거의 항상 나쁜 뜻이에요. '정경 유착'(정치와 경제의 유착)처럼 써요. 단순히 친한 사이는 '친밀', '가깝다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '유착' describes a relationship in which parties stick together to share improper gains, so it is almost always negative. A typical use is '정경 유착' (collusion between politics and business). For simply being close, say '친밀하다' or '가깝다'.
